title: Lucha Libre Week: AAA Suspends Rey Mysterio as GM After Hall of Fame Chaos, and Máscara Dorada Closes Out CMLL's Tuesday Night
excerpt: AAA closed its Heroes Inmortales series with Marisela Peña's Hall of Fame induction turning into a family showdown that ended with Rey Mysterio suspended indefinitely, while CMLL's week ended with Máscara Dorada winning the Arena México main event.
content:
Mexican lucha libre delivered one of its biggest weeks of the year, with a Hall of Fame ceremony that turned into a front-office earthquake in AAA and a full slate of CMLL shows across Mexico City and Puebla.

AAA closed its Heroes Inmortales series with its third and final week, which aired Friday, Nov. 7, on Fox in Latin America and the WWE YouTube channel. The episode was taped Oct. 24 at the Gimnasio Olímpico Juan de la Barrera in Mexico City.

The night belonged to Marisela Peña, who was inducted into the AAA Hall of Fame by Rey Mysterio, who praised her leadership in guiding the company into its new era under WWE following the death of her brother and company founder Antonio Peña. The celebration did not last. Peña's son, Dorian Roldán, interrupted the ceremony and announced that AAA's higher authorities had indefinitely suspended Mysterio as general manager, citing complaints from Triplemanía 34 — including fostering unsafe working conditions that led to El Hijo del Vikingo's injury, attacking Omos, and abusing his authority by counting an unauthorized three-count in the AAA Mega Championship match.

In the ring, Bravo Americano won the opening triple threat over Cruz del Toro and Kento, and the grudge match between Abismo Negro Jr. and El Fiscal ended in disqualification after Abismo used the steel steps at ringside. Pimpinela Escarlata also cut a fiery backstage promo challenging Omos to a fight.

Over in CMLL, the week closed Tuesday, Nov. 10, at Arena México, where Máscara Dorada defeated Villano III Jr. in the main event, finishing him with a shooting star press. Earlier on the card, Persephone, Reyna Isis and Keyra defeated Tessa Blanchard, Garra Negra and Lluvia, and Los Bestia del Diablo — Akuma and Gemelo Diablo I and II — beat Fuego, Volcano and Dulce Gardenia after Akuma's low blow on Volcano. A singles challenge between Akuma and Volcano followed and was accepted, though no date was confirmed.

The women's rivalry carried through the week. On Monday, Nov. 9, at Arena Puebla, Persephone beat Tessa Blanchard in a lightning match during Lunes Clásico, where Guerreros Laguneros — Gran Guerrero, Stuka Jr. and Último Guerrero — also beat Galeón Fantasma in the main event.

Friday's Viernes Espectacular on Nov. 6 saw Bandido, Titán and Neón defeat Soberano Jr., Averno and Bárbaro Cavernario, while Las Fieras del Ring beat Los Depredadores — Volador Jr. and Vegas Depredador — by disqualification. On Saturday, Nov. 7, at Sábado de Coliseo, Neón and Blue Panther defeated Averno and Ángel de Oro, and Euforia beat Gemelo Diablo I.

Sources: Pro Wrestling Dot Net, Nov. 7-8, 2026; Fightful, Nov. 8, 2026; Wrestling Attitude, Nov. 9, 2026; The DDT, Nov. 8, 2026; Lucha Central, Nov. 3, 2026; The Wrestling Voice (Morning Bell), Nov. 11, 2026; BodySlam, Nov. 6, 2026.
